sentences: **PSV0** (DXBC) gives NumThreads (128×1×1 in the corpus), MaxOutputVertices/Primitives (128/128) and the topology (triangles).

System inputs, from Mesa's RADV setup for mesh as NGG on GFX10.3: v5 = first launch vertex ID of the lane (the "vertex_id" slot), `linearGroupIndex * NumThreads + LocalInvocationIndex` with the linear index from WorkgroupId/NumWorkgroups; all 9,282/9,282 corpus mesh shaders read `v5` once with `v_readfirstlane_b32 sX, v5` and use `sX` only via `s_lshr_b32 D, sX, 7` to recover the group index (NumThreads is 128 in the corpus), matching TomBox's mesh ABI (`gid.x * numThreads + gi`) on 1D launches.

GPU-checked with `runtime/test/shaders/ms_v5_workgroup.asm` (24/24 groups exact on RTX 4060 Ti and RTX 3080, and on an RTX 4050 Laptop and an AMD Radeon 740M (RADV)); still unverified on Xbox hardware: the low 7 bits of `v5` on lanes 1..127 and whether 3D `DispatchMesh` flattens XYZ or uses X only.

The merged-wave-info SGPR (s3 in this ABI) = wave ID << 24, from LocalInvocationIndex >> 6; `v_mbcnt` lanes = LocalInvocationIndex & 63; user data in s16.. as usual. 1,473 of 1,500 sampled mesh shaders read exactly v5, and the rest only add loop-carried registers.
Exports: on NGG, thread t exports vertex t (`pos0`, `paramN`) and primitive t (`prim`).
They're staged per invocation; an all-`off` export is the dummy a wave with no vertices must issue, and writes nothing.
`s_sendmsg GS_ALLOC_REQ` (m0 = prims << 12 \| verts, sent by thread 0) stores the counts in a workgroup variable.

At shader end, in uniform control flow: workgroup barrier, `OpSetMeshOutputsEXT(min(verts, max), min(prims, max))`, then each thread writes its staged vertex (Position + Location N) and primitive (`PrimitiveTriangleIndicesEXT` = bits [8:0], [18:10], [28:20]; `CullPrimitiveEXT` = bit 31).

`pos1..pos3` clip/cull distances are staged per invocation and emitted in a per-vertex `Block` output struct (`Position` + `ClipDistance`/`CullDistance` arrays, `VK_EXT_mesh_shader`) when used, keeping the standalone `%ms_out_pos` layout unchanged for shaders without `pos1+`.

The distances are copied to that struct one float at a time, not as a whole array: SPIRV-Cross 1.4.363.0 turns a whole-array store into a mesh output into a C array assignment that Metal rejects (SHADER-155; `ms_clip` then compiles and draws its 2048/4096 pixels in a native Metal mesh draw on an Apple A18 Pro).

GPU-checked with `runtime/test/shaders/ms_tri.asm` (`VKH_MESH=1 vk_harness`), built from the game's own idioms (thread ID from s3 and mbcnt across two waves, thread-0 ALLOC_REQ, per-thread exports): 0 error on every pixel.
